title: Caruso with piano and orchestra
work: Ruggero Leoncavallo: Recitar!… Vesti la giubba
question: What changes in Caruso’s lament when an orchestra takes the place of the piano?
intro: Canio has discovered his wife’s betrayal, and the paying audience is waiting for him to make them laugh. In Leoncavallo’s Pagliacci, he orders himself to put on his costume and powder his face. Caruso recorded the aria with Salvatore Cottone at the piano in Milan in 1902, then with an orchestra in New York in 1907.

recordings.label: Enrico Caruso, Salvatore Cottone
recordings.note: One tenor and one pianist: Cottone supplies the whole accompaniment in this Milan performance of 30 November 1902.

recordings.label: Enrico Caruso with orchestra
recordings.note: An orchestra surrounds Canio’s lament in the later Victor recording, made in New York.

passages.label: Voice and piano
passages.note: The tenor carries Canio’s lament above the piano accompaniment. His words tell the clown to put on his costume.

passages.label: The phrase rises
passages.note: The vocal phrase climbs and subsides; the accompaniment carries the music between the tenor’s breaths.

passages.label: The last plea
passages.note: The tenor’s line rises again, stretching towards the aria’s final phrases over the accompaniment.

passages.label: Towards the close
passages.note: The last vocal phrases lead towards the accompaniment’s closing bars.
